topic: Expression value from a linear constraint
problem: If 2x+y=20, what is the value of 8x^2+18x+8xy+9y+2y^2?

bad.why: One convenient pair such as x=0, y=20 gives 980 but does not show that every pair on the line gives the same value.

algebraFirst.description: Either spots the regrouping 2(2x+y)^2+9(2x+y) (a hard factoring insight) or plugs one convenient pair like x=0, y=20 without showing every pair gives the same value.

explanationNotes: Explain that 2x+y=20 lets every y be replaced by 20-2x, and the resulting graph is a flat horizontal line at 980: the expression has the same value at every point on the line, so 980 is the answer and not a lucky pick of x and y.
notes: Paraphrase of Bedrock Prep hard Problem 23, One Variable in Disguise. Recognize the expression as 2(2x+y)^2+9(2x+y). Substituting 20 yields 2*400+9*20=980. A calculator route can verify the identity at multiple values, but must explain why the expression depends only on 2x+y. Category index: https://www.bedrockprep.com/problems
